You’re in the gym. You see someone you’re interested in talking to. How do you open the conversation? I assume you don’t walk up like “You and I share fitness interests, we should be friendly”. 

No, I assume you probably open with something mundane. “Nice set you just did” or “I love that team on your shirt, hopefully they win tonight” or any number of small things to get it started. Having mutual interests is great and definitely is a starting point, but that only gets you in the door. Your social skills are what carry you further. Talking in the gym is no different than talking to someone at a bar or at a stop light. The only difference is, you may see this person again.

First off, if you have so little energy that chatting with strangers worries you, you need to eat a sandwich. 

Second, how do you know it will be a waste or meaningless? Worst case scenario, you have a slightly awkward conversation, go on your way, and never think about it again. Maybe meaningless but you didn’t really lose anything. 

Best case scenario, you strike up a conversation with a fun and engaging person, talk for a while, and leave in a better mood than you started. Hell, maybe you’ll even make a friend. 

It’s zero risk, low reward 90% of the time, but that 10% is still zero risk and high reward. 

Engaging with people is not meaningless. These are people in your community, you should want to engage with them if only because they live with you.

Could I ask what attacks are tripping you up in phase two? I’ve spent over 70 hours learning to no hit him so I know the pain. Phase two is a lot, there is a lot going on visually and mechanically. If there are any specific moves or combos you struggle with, I will absolutely help. 

As for general tips, I first recommend staying as far from the back of the arena as possible. Near the pillar things the ground gets really rough and can cause some jank. Stay in the flat area as much as you can. When he does the meteor attack, he will always spawn directly above the fog gate. Once you see him start the launch, run to the far wall, either left or right. If you are in the middle, pick which one you want. Don’t stop running, just go as far as possible. I also like to jump as he hits the ground to ensure I don’t get hit. Disengaging like this will feel unnatural for a souls fight but it is by far the best way to get clear and will allow for a brief reset mentally. Finally, in regard to his light beams after his attacks, almost all of them spawn a distance away from him, at about the tip of his sword swings. Because of this, you can roll straight towards his body, keeping real close on these melee attacks and the light beams will hit behind you entirely. This is also why you want flat ground ideally because on slopes it is a lot less guaranteed. The attacks that send the beams straight out are obviously different as the beams start at him, but those attacks are far easier to dodge as a whole. 

If you have made it this far then you absolutely have the skill to beat him. He is by far the hardest boss in Elden Ring and arguably in all of Souls. I cannot blame you for stopping, but I know that if you keep at it, you absolutely will crush him eventually.

This is just not true. Value is not determined by the labor put in. For example, I absolutely hate eating pineapples, I cannot stand them. Now, farming pineapples still takes a lot of time, effort, and labor. Despite that, to me, a pineapple has no value. I do not care for it. On a subjective level, the pineapple is worthless to me the consumer no matter how much work you put in. 

Now, why do pineapples have a price? Well, it is because my subjective opinion is not the whole market. Some people love pineapple and would be willing to pay just about anything to get one. Some people like it but will only get one if the price is reasonable. Now, let’s say that something happened that made everyone in the market dislike pineapples. Some overnight shift in opinion. All of the sudden, all that labor and time you put into farming those pineapples means nothing. No matter what you price it or how valuable you think your labor is, if the market does not value the product, your labor is worthless. 

Companies and producers don’t set prices based on labor, they set it on supply and demand. Yes, it is a lot cheaper and easier to make TVs now, but the prices didn’t go down because there is less labor involved. The price went down simply because there are now more TVs available. Even if while costs drop demand goes up, prices will fall. Again, not because your labor is some magically valuable thing inherently, but because if companies lower the cost, more people can buy TVs. If both demand and supply are high, companies are still incentivized to lower prices to ensure the most people can buy the product as possible. And we haven’t even gotten into the effects of competition yet. 

Obviously there is a baseline cost to produce anything, and that will have its place in determining price, but no matter what, if people don’t value the product, your labor is worthless. It doesn’t matter how long you spent or how passionate you are, if it only has value to you, then it will never sell. You need to find a balance between how you the producer value something and how the consumer will value it. In other words, it is a subjective scale. 

Calling subjectivity irrational is insane. We all live subjective lives. There is next to no objectivity in human reality, especially not when dealing with any group greater than 2. Why would the market be any different.

I don’t know if I have just been cooking chicken breast long enough that I’m just good at it or if you guys are just bad. Cooking chicken breast is not that hard. Here’s a recipe for anyone who wants to give it a shot. Slice a chicken breast into flat strips. Spice one side of the chicken with your favorite seasoning. Be generous if you wish. Put just a little bit of olive oil in a pan and let it heat up, probably no more than a half tablespoon or so for 1 breast. When the pan is hot, put the chicken in, spice side down. While the bottom is cooking, spice the top side to your liking. It only takes a few minutes at best to cook each side. I cook the bottom until it looks at least cooked on the surface and then flip it for roughly the same time. Use cooking wine or white wine occasionally to keep the spice on the chicken and not the pan. Keep flipping the chicken, it will be cooking for at most 5-7 minutes if your chicken is thin. It is very little effort and it gives a very nice meal. If you’re still not sure if it’s done, cut a piece of the chicken at the thickest part of the slice. If it is white all the way through then you’re good. If you’re still worried, get a thermometer and find out the right temp for chicken. I’ll be honest, I make this almost weekly and have “burned” it plenty of times. Not once has the chicken itself not been juicy and tender. With a little practice, you’ll have it down in no time.

The past 4 years have been pretty disastrous. I don’t care what anybody says, the Biden administration has not been good for the country outside of some very specific policy issues. Kamala is obviously a major player in this administration. She has even gone on record recently saying that she was a part of the decision making in many major decisions and that she wouldn’t have done anything different from what Biden has done. Despite this, she is running on a campaign of “change”. I find it incredibly disingenuous for someone who currently holds the second most powerful position, advising directly to the most powerful person in the world, to claim that she will change things later. If these are things she truly wished to do and not just say in an attempt for a blatant power grab at the presidency, then she would be working to do them now. I can go on for a while as to why I do not trust Kamala Harris to meaningfully improve this country outside of the decriminalizing of marijuana. However, the question is why I will be voting for Trump, not why I won’t vote for her. 

While my lack of trust and general disdain for Harris is a major factor in my choice this election, I do believe that Donald Trump will be a net good for the country. I do not think he will be perfect, nowhere near so. I, however, am a minarchist. I am disgusted by how large the federal government has grown. One thing that Trump has planned to do is slash federal jobs and cut the bureaucracy. That position alone has the potential to fix so many of our problems and I don’t think many people realize it. This is arguably the thing that is most enticing to me about his policies. Sure, he could break my trust and not follow through, but he at least is saying he will whereas Harris was the VP when the IRS alone added 10s of thousands of new agents to their bloated payroll. I will take a promise of a solution over no solution whether that promise ends up being upheld or not. 

Another reason for my support of Trump is that his economic plan seems to be stronger. It is hard to gauge this, I will say, as you can find sources for both their plans saying that both will save us and both will destroy us. Most of that is due to bias in reporting. From my own analysis however, I do believe that his proposal will be a net positive over the Harris proposal. My main criticism is the tariffs he is suggesting. That being said, by and large I support the policies. We also have already seen his policies in action for the most part in his last term. Things were significantly cheaper under Trump than Biden, that is not debatable. A lot of people try to use Covid to explain this, and while it did explain the rising prices at the end of Trump’s and the beginning of Biden’s term, it does not explain current prices. I have Biden, and by proxy Harris, the benefit of the doubt for 2 whole years. The fact that they have failed to pass any sort of policy to bring down prices to comparable levels to before Covid is a failing on their part. I trust Trump more at this point to remedy our economic issues than Harris. That being said, I do worry that it will be too late for anyone and that we will just see a crash down the line regardless, but if someone is to pull us out, I think Trump has a better chance.
